1999-09-03: Ariel Sharon wins the leadership of Israel's opposition Likud party.
2000-09-28: Israeli hardliner Ariel Sharon leads a group of Likud politicians into the sacred area in east Jerusalem known to Muslims as al-Haram al-Sharif and to Jews as the Temple Mount.
2000-10-02: World leaders condemn Ariel Sharon's visit to a holy site in Jerusalem, which triggered five days of violence.
2000-10-12: Ariel Sharon, leader of the opposition Likud party, was still considering Prime Minister Ehud Barak's request to join an emergency national unity coalition following the violent collapse of the peace process.
2001-01-05: Opinion polls indicate Ariel Sharon holds a massive lead ahead of the February 6 direct election for Israeli prime minister.
2001-01-30: Ariel Sharon is widely expected to be elected Israeli prime minister in the upcoming election, despite his role as defense minister during the 1982 Sabra and Shatila massacre.
2001-02-06: Israelis vote in a general election widely expected to result in a landslide victory for Likud leader Ariel Sharon over Prime Minister Ehud Barak.
Exit polls project Ariel Sharon winning Israel's prime ministerial election over Ehud Barak by 59.5 percent to 40.5 percent.
Ariel Sharon wins Israel's election for prime minister with 62.5% of the vote, defeating Ehud Barak.
2001-02-07: Ariel Sharon is elected prime minister of Israel, prompting cautious and critical reactions from world leaders.
2001-02-08: Ariel Sharon, Israel's prime minister-elect, pledges not to resume peace talks until violence ends, following a suspected car bomb explosion in west Jerusalem.
2001-02-10: Ariel Sharon, the new Israeli Prime Minister, makes a dramatic bid to woo senior left-wing figures, including Shimon Peres as Foreign Minister and Ehud Barak as Defence Minister, into his government.
2001-02-11: Labour party splits over the prospect of an alliance with hardline prime minister-elect Ariel Sharon, as Shimon Peres declares willingness to serve as foreign minister in a national unity coalition while other Labour figures prepare to exit.
2001-02-13: Prime minister-elect Ariel Sharon is on the verge of stitching up a coalition deal ahead of the installation of his new government.
2001-02-17: Ehud Barak agrees to serve as defence minister under incoming Likud prime minister Ariel Sharon.
2001-02-26: Israel's Labour party voted to join prime minister-elect Ariel Sharon's unity government.
2001-03-06: Ariel Sharon told Israel's parliament he had successfully formed a broad-based national unity government and is ready to take power the next day.
2001-03-07: Ariel Sharon is sworn in as Israel's prime minister, leading a broad-based national unity coalition government.
2001-04-15: Ariel Sharon's government escalated military action against the Palestinians, including helicopter gunship strikes on Palestinian security barracks, abductions in Palestinian areas, and political assassinations in Gaza.
2001-04-17: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon sent troops into a Palestinian autonomous area in the Gaza Strip, destroying four Palestinian border posts, before withdrawing them less than 24 hours later under US pressure.
2001-04-18: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon ordered a withdrawal from northern Gaza after US criticism, then launched a further incursion into Gaza the next day.
2001-05-11: A senior aide to Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon resigns in anger over the special envoy post given to Sharon's son Omri.
2001-05-22: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon rejects the Mitchell report's call for an immediate freeze on illegal Jewish settlements in the West Bank and Gaza, while calling for a ceasefire.
2001-05-25: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon again calls for a Palestinian ceasefire, hours after a car bomb killed three people in Hadera.
2001-06-14: Israeli officials criticized the BBC over a Panorama programme concluding that Prime Minister Ariel Sharon could be tried for war crimes related to the 1982 Sabra and Shatila massacres.
2001-07-11: A Dutch general practitioner calls for Ariel Sharon to be brought to justice for war crimes, alleging he coordinated the 1982 Phalangist militia entry into the Sabra and Shatila refugee camps that led to the murder of over 2,000 civilians.
2001-08-14: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon warned that Palestinians would lose "additional assets" as Israeli forces moved toward an incursion around Bethlehem.
2001-09-16: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon rebuffs US calls for ceasefire talks and orders the third invasion of a Palestinian-ruled city in less than a week, setting new conditions for truce talks.
2001-10-04: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon renounced the week-old Middle East ceasefire and accused Washington of sacrificing Israel to win Arab support for a broad war coalition.
2001-10-16: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon attempted to shore up his coalition government after the resignation of two rightwing ministers.
2001-10-22: Ariel Sharon's government conducted a military invasion into Palestinian areas including Ramallah, Jenin, Bethlehem, Beit Jala, Beit Sahour, Qalqilya and Tulkarm, beginning a gradual reoccupation of Palestinian-controlled areas.
2001-11-26: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon replaces Israel's most seasoned negotiator with hardline former general Meir Dagan as lead negotiator ahead of a US peace mission.
2002-01-04: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon informed US peace envoy Anthony Zinni of the interception of the Karine-A, a vessel allegedly carrying illicit weapons for the Palestinian Authority, before Zinni met with Yasser Arafat.
2002-01-24: Elie Hobeika, a potential key witness in the Belgian war crimes case against Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon, was killed by a bomb in Beirut along with three bodyguards.
2002-01-28: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon is being urged to create a "hermetic" security cordon dividing Arab east from Jewish west Jerusalem, following a suicide bombing in west Jerusalem.
2002-02-01: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon says in a newspaper interview that Israel should have eliminated Yasser Arafat during the 1982 invasion of Lebanon and regrets not doing so, while stating Israel has no intention of harming Arafat now.
Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon's public approval rating dropped to its lowest in months amid a petition by 104 combat reservist officers refusing to serve in the occupied territories.
2002-02-22: Ariel Sharon’s siege of Yasser Arafat in Ramallah is described as facing risks and resistance similar to his 1982 siege of West Beirut, with no clear new event beyond the ongoing siege.
2002-02-28: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon launched the most concerted effort to crush Palestinian militants on their home terrain since the uprising began, as the Israeli army stormed the Balata and Jenin refugee camps in the West Bank.
2002-03-01: An opinion poll finds that for the first time a majority of Israelis (53%) are dissatisfied with Prime Minister Ariel Sharon's performance.
2002-03-03: Ariel Sharon's strongarm tactics of sending the Israeli army into refugee camps in Balata and Jenin backfired, producing more bloodshed, innocent victims, and bitterness, with further Palestinian attacks following.
2002-03-06: US Secretary of State Colin Powell calls on Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon to reconsider his policies, saying declaring war on Palestinians will not work.
2002-03-13: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon vowed to continue the deadliest military offensive against the Palestinians in 20 years, overriding his defence minister’s protests and pushing the assault on Ramallah hours before the arrival of US envoy Anthony Zinni.
2002-03-15: Ariel Sharon is criticized for ordering Israeli military incursions into Palestinian areas, described as the country's biggest military operation in 20 years.
2002-03-26: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon demanded that Washington allow the possible exile of Yasser Arafat and toughened his demands on barring Arafat from returning if he attended the Arab League summit.
2002-03-27: Arab newspapers report that Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon has effectively ruled out the Saudi peace initiative and is pursuing a brute-force policy that complicates US diplomacy.
2002-03-29: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon launched a sweeping military offensive in the West Bank, calling up 31,000 reservists.
2002-04-02: Israeli warplanes, armour and infantry launch a huge attack on Bethlehem as Ariel Sharon pushes ahead with the second phase of his five-day long assault on Palestinian targets.
2002-04-04: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon's offensive in the West Bank destroyed Palestinian Authority institutions and targeted Yasser Arafat's compound, which critics said aimed to erase the eight-year period of Arafat's rule.
2002-04-08: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon said he intended to complete the military operation against Yasser Arafat's "regime of terror," defying US calls to pull troops out of the West Bank immediately.
2002-04-09: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon vowed to continue the military offensive after 13 Israeli soldiers were killed in Jenin.
2002-04-14: Ariel Sharon wages a military operation on the West Bank, named 'Operation Defensive Shield', which is described as a replay of his 1982 invasion of Lebanon.

Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon threatened to storm Yasser Arafat's headquarters to capture the killers of far-right cabinet minister Rechavam Zeevi, potentially derailing US Secretary of State Colin Powell's Middle East peace mission.
2002-04-16: Labour MP Gerald Kaufman accused Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon of being a "war criminal" and using "methods of barbarism" against Palestinians during a Commons debate on the Middle East crisis.
2002-04-17: President George W. Bush declared Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon a "man of peace."
2002-04-19: Palestinians hope the UN Security Council's decision to send a fact-finding mission to the Jenin refugee camp could lead to an international criminal trial of Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon and other senior figures.
2002-04-21: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon said the first stage of Israel's offensive had ended as tanks redeployed around Nablus and Ramallah, while the siege of Yasser Arafat's headquarters continued.
2002-04-23: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon decided to reject the UN fact-finding mission to the Jenin refugee camp, reversing Israel's earlier commitment and prompting a US rebuke.
2002-04-28: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon's government threatened to block a UN investigation into the Israeli assault on the Jenin refugee camp, with the UN team expected to arrive in Tel Aviv that evening after delays.
2002-05-08: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon returns from Washington facing options including expelling Yasser Arafat, invading the Gaza Strip, or escalating raids on West Bank towns, with no ceasefire among the choices.
2002-05-12: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon was publicly defied and humiliated when Binyamin Netanyahu led Likud party members to reject the foundation of a Palestinian state.
2002-06-05: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon came under intense pressure to reoccupy the entire West Bank and Gaza and expel Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat after a Palestinian suicide car bombing killed 16 people.
2002-06-08: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon flew to Washington to persuade President Bush against a return to negotiations with the Palestinians.
2002-06-10: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon met with US President George W. Bush at the White House and won US backing for Israel's demand that the Palestinian leadership be overhauled before meaningful peace talks can begin.
2002-06-24: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon said the army was preparing "massive activity" against Hamas in the Gaza Strip, following a helicopter missile strike that killed six Palestinians.
2002-09-03: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon ordered military and emergency preparations for a possible Iraqi counterstrike to be completed by November 1.
2002-09-28: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon orders a siege of Yasser Arafat's Ramallah compound, demanding the handover of alleged terrorists.
2002-10-14: Ariel Sharon is quoted as regretting his failure to kill Yasir Arafat in Beirut during the 1982 Israeli invasion of Lebanon.
2002-10-30: Israel's national unity coalition government collapsed after Labour party ministers resigned over a budget dispute, forcing Prime Minister Ariel Sharon to rely on rightwing minority parties.
Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon met with Labour leader Binyamin Ben-Eliezer to discuss a compromise to prevent the coalition government from collapsing over the budget.
2002-10-31: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon appoints former army chief Shaul Mofaz as defence minister after Labour ministers resigned from the coalition government.
2002-11-01: Ariel Sharon invites his rival Binyamin Netanyahu to join the cabinet as foreign minister in an effort to neutralize the threat to his position as prime minister.
2002-11-05: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon survived three no-confidence votes in parliament, with parliament also approving Shaul Mofaz as the new defence minister.
2002-11-07: Israeli Foreign Minister Binyamin Netanyahu said in an interview that Ariel Sharon's leadership had left Israel in dire straits, as Netanyahu planned to challenge Sharon for the Likud party leadership.
2002-11-13: Binyamin Netanyahu secures a Likud arrangement making him next in line to succeed Ariel Sharon, though Sharon’s aides say it does not guarantee Netanyahu a leading role in the next government if Sharon is returned to office.
2002-11-18: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon was considering razing Palestinian homes to create a secure corridor for Jewish settlers in the West Bank.
2003-01-14: Israel's opposition Labour party rules out rejoining a government headed by Ariel Sharon after the general election, while Sharon rules out working with religious parties.
2003-01-29: Ariel Sharon threatened to call another election if Labour refuses to join a coalition government, saying he would not establish a narrow rightwing government under any circumstances.
2003-02-03: Israeli Labour party leader Amram Mitzna told Ariel Sharon he would not join a coalition government unless Sharon agreed to shut Jewish settlements in the Gaza Strip and begin negotiations with the Palestinians.
2003-02-13: Labour party leader Amram Mitzna softened his stance towards joining a national unity government led by Ariel Sharon, with Mitzna and Shinui leader Tommy Lapid set to meet to discuss joining a Sharon-led cabinet.
2003-02-21: Ariel Sharon’s Likud party reached a tentative agreement with the secular Shinui party and the National Religious Party to form a coalition government.
2003-02-23: Israeli Labour party ruled out joining a national unity government with Ariel Sharon after he insisted on including the rightwing National Religious party as a coalition partner.
2003-02-26: Ariel Sharon sacks Benjamin Netanyahu as foreign minister and replaces him with Silvan Shalom, in a move apparently aimed at reassuring the United States about the new government's seriousness in pursuing a peace agreement with the Palestinians.
2003-03-30: Ariel Sharon's coalition government survives its first crisis after ultra-orthodox parties refused to attend a cabinet meeting in protest at a de facto lifting of the ban on working on the Sabbath.
2003-06-04: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon endorses the establishment of an independent Palestinian state at a summit in Aqaba, Jordan, and pledges to dismantle unauthorized settlement outposts.
2003-06-11: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon ordered a failed assassination attempt on Hamas political leader Abdel-Aziz al-Rantissi, which was followed by a Hamas suicide bombing in Jerusalem that killed 16 people.
2003-07-20: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon met with Palestinian Prime Minister Mahmoud Abbas, who described the meeting as "extremely disappointing" after Israel deferred action on Palestinian demands, including prisoner releases, until after Sharon's visit to Washington.
2003-07-29: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon is preparing to meet US President George W. Bush at the White House, with Israel claiming it is fulfilling commitments made at the Aqaba summit to dismantle unauthorized settlement outposts.
2003-12-18: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon delivered an ultimatum to the Palestinians to act against terrorists or he will embark on a "unilateral separation" plan within months.
2004-01-04: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon ordered the army to remove two inhabited Jewish outposts in the West Bank, drawing criticism from both the religious right and the left.
2004-01-05: Ariel Sharon was heckled and booed by members of his own Likud party as he defended his plan for a partial withdrawal from occupied territories and the dismantling of some Jewish settlements.
2004-01-11: Tens of thousands of Israeli settlers and supporters rally in Tel Aviv to denounce Ariel Sharon's plan to remove Jewish outposts in the West Bank and Gaza.
2004-01-21: Israeli businessman David Appel is indicted for allegedly paying hundreds of thousands of dollars to Ariel Sharon's family for political favors, leaving Sharon one step away from corruption charges and being forced from office.
2004-01-27: Jewish settlers say they rejected an offer by Ariel Sharon to limit settlement evacuations in return for cooperation with his unilateral withdrawal plan, while Sharon denies planning to evacuate seven Jewish settlements.
2004-02-02: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon told his Likud Party that he plans to dismantle Israeli settlements in the Gaza Strip, saying he had ordered planning for the evacuation of the 17 Gaza settlements.
2004-02-18: The US tacitly approves Ariel Sharon's plan for unilateral disengagement from the Palestinians, setting conditions including a refusal to let Israel formally annex Jewish settlements in the West Bank.
2004-03-02: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon is reported to back a total withdrawal of Israeli settlers and soldiers from the Gaza Strip, though no final decision has been made.
2004-03-10: Israeli and Palestinian prime ministers Ariel Sharon and Ahmed Qureia agree to meet next week, their first meeting in more than six months.
2004-04-02: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon threatens in media interviews to take action against Palestinian Authority chairman Yasser Arafat, though it is unclear what action he proposes.
2004-04-10: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon struggled to garner support for his proposal that Israel unilaterally withdraw from the Gaza Strip, with his "disengagement" plan expected to face a Likud party vote next month.
2004-05-27: Ariel Sharon is reported to have shelved a plan for a cabinet vote on an Israeli withdrawal from Gaza.
2004-05-28: Ariel Sharon reveals a new four-stage plan for evacuating settlements in the Gaza Strip, with the cabinet to vote on the first phase the following Sunday.
2004-05-30: Ariel Sharon threatened to dismiss ministers opposed to his Gaza disengagement plan and to take unprecedented political steps to force it through, staking his premiership on the plan amid a power struggle with Binyamin Netanyahu.
2004-06-04: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon sacked two hardline ministers from the far-right National Union party in an attempt to win cabinet support for his plan to remove all Jewish settlers from the Gaza Strip.
2004-06-06: The Israeli government accepted the removal of some Jewish settlements from occupied Palestinian territories, paving the way for Ariel Sharon to fulfill a pledge to dismantle all settlements in Gaza by the end of next year.
2004-06-15: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon was cleared of corruption charges when the attorney general decided there was insufficient evidence to indict him and his son Gilad over the Greek Island affair.
2004-07-12: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon invited the moderate Labour party into his fragile coalition government and warned rebels in his Likud party that he would call early elections if they tried to block the move.
2004-08-18: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon suffered a blow when his Likud party voted to prevent him from inviting new partners into the government, though he vowed to proceed with negotiations to expand the coalition.
2004-08-20: Ariel Sharon was almost certainly invoking Likud members' adulation of Menachem Begin to win support for his disengagement plan.
2004-08-31: Prime Minister Ariel Sharon outlines an accelerated plan to evacuate Jewish settlements in the Gaza Strip, proposing that the withdrawal begin as early as next year.
2004-10-22: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon faces accusations of betrayal from within his Likud party over his Gaza withdrawal plan ahead of a Knesset vote.
2004-10-24: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon seeks Knesset approval for parts of his plan to withdraw from Jewish settlements in the Gaza Strip and northern West Bank.
2004-10-25: Ariel Sharon opened a parliamentary debate on his plan to remove Jewish settlers from Gaza, defending the "disengagement plan" ahead of a vote expected to split his Likud party.
2004-10-26: Israel's parliament voted 67-45 to approve Ariel Sharon's unilateral disengagement plan to remove Jewish settlements from the Gaza Strip and a small part of the West Bank.
2004-10-27: The Knesset approves Ariel Sharon's disengagement plan from Gaza.

Ariel Sharon rejects calls from four cabinet ministers to hold a referendum on his unilateral disengagement plan for removing Jewish settlers from the Gaza Strip and part of the West Bank, saying he will not give in to pressures, threats, or ultimatums.
2004-11-25: Lieut-Gen Rafael Eitan, who with then-defence minister Ariel Sharon conceived the 1982 Peace for Galilee plan to dislodge the PLO from southern Lebanon, has drowned aged 75.
2004-12-01: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon's government faces collapse after his main coalition partner, the Shinui party, causes the defeat of the annual budget in parliament, prompting Sharon to sack Shinui ministers from his cabinet.
2004-12-09: Ariel Sharon wins backing from his ruling Likud party to invite the Labour opposition into the government, appearing to assure his Gaza withdrawal plan.
2004-12-11: Israel's opposition Labour party began talks with Prime Minister Ariel Sharon's Likud party about joining its coalition, a partnership aimed at promoting a military withdrawal from Gaza.
2005-02-20: The Israeli cabinet approved Ariel Sharon's plan to pull out of the Gaza Strip and a small part of the West Bank, authorizing the first ever removal of Jewish settlers from the Palestinian territories.
2005-03-27: Ariel Sharon averts a political crisis by winning opposition support for his budget, removing the last major legislative obstacle to closing settlements in Gaza and four isolated ones in the northern West Bank.
2005-04-04: Jewish settlers split over Ariel Sharon's plan to pull out of the Gaza Strip as their leaders meet the prime minister to discuss terms for a mass relocation.
2005-04-11: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon brushed off President George W. Bush's warning against further West Bank settlement growth, indicating Israel would continue to solidify its hold on areas it considers strategically important.
2005-05-01: Natan Sharansky resigns from Ariel Sharon's government in protest at the plan to evacuate settlements in Gaza and the northern West Bank.
2005-05-08: Ariel Sharon says he will delay the forcible removal of Jewish settlers from the Gaza Strip until mid-August, after a traditional Jewish mourning period ends on August 14.
2005-06-09: Israel's supreme court ruled that Prime Minister Ariel Sharon's Gaza withdrawal plan is constitutional, removing the last legal obstacle to the pullback scheduled for mid-August.
2005-07-20: A parliamentary vote to delay Ariel Sharon's Gaza disengagement plan failed, and police contained anti-disengagement protesters at a campsite.
2005-08-04: Ariel Sharon condemns the killing of four Arab civilians by an Israeli soldier as a "despicable act by a bloodthirsty terrorist."
2005-08-07: Israeli Finance Minister Binyamin Netanyahu resigned from the government over Prime Minister Ariel Sharon's plan to withdraw from settlements in Gaza.
2005-08-15: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon describes the abandonment of Gaza settlements as a "painful step" but essential for Israel's future in a televised speech as the eviction of settlers begins.
Ariel Sharon says that if the Palestinians reach out a hand in peace, Israel will respond with an olive branch, but if they choose fire, Israel will respond with fire more severe than ever.
2005-08-18: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon’s disengagement plan gained public support as soldiers and policemen completed the removal of Jewish families from all but four of the 21 doomed Gaza settlements ahead of schedule.
Israel began demolishing evacuated homes in Jewish settlements in the Gaza Strip and troops forcibly entered synagogues amid protests against Ariel Sharon's disengagement plan.
2005-08-20: Ariel Sharon accuses settler leaders of causing unnecessary suffering for political gain during the Gaza Strip pullout.
2005-08-23: Israeli forces completed the evacuation of the last 25 Jewish settlements in the Gaza Strip and West Bank under Ariel Sharon's disengagement plan.
2005-08-29: Binyamin Netanyahu launched a bid to unseat Israeli prime minister Ariel Sharon by seeking the leadership of the ruling Likud party.
2005-09-26: Ariel Sharon narrowly survived an attempt to force an early leadership election in the ruling Likud party, in retaliation for his demolition of Jewish settlements in Gaza.
2005-10-26: Ariel Sharon announced a "broad and continuous" offensive in the occupied territories and warned that Palestinians have no hope of winning independence until they combat armed Islamist groups, a day after an Islamic Jihad suicide bombing killed five Israelis.
2005-11-10: Ariel Sharon is likely to be forced into an early general election after Shimon Peres was unexpectedly toppled as leader of the Labour party, his main coalition partner.
2005-11-17: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon agrees to call a general election in about three months after Labour party leader Amir Peretz threatened a no-confidence vote.
2005-11-20: Ariel Sharon decides to leave the Likud party he founded and force new elections, reportedly to form a new centrist party.
2005-11-21: Ariel Sharon announces his departure from the ruling Likud party and runs for prime minister at the head of a new party, Kadima.
2005-11-30: Shimon Peres resigned from Israel's Labour party to support Ariel Sharon's re-election, saying Sharon offers the best opportunity for peace with the Palestinians.
2005-12-14: Ariel Sharon denied a Newsweek report that he was willing to compromise on Jerusalem and give up 90% of the West Bank in a future peace deal with the Palestinians.
2005-12-18: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon suffered a mild stroke and was rushed to Jerusalem's Hadassah hospital for treatment.
2005-12-20: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon is to be released from hospital following a mild stroke.
2005-12-26: Doctors at a Jerusalem hospital said that 77-year-old Ariel Sharon will undergo a minor operation next month to close a small hole in his heart.
2006-01-03: Likud party leader Benjamin Netanyahu ordered his cabinet ministers to quit the Israeli government, six weeks after Prime Minister Ariel Sharon resigned as Likud leader and set up the centrist Kadima party.
2006-01-04: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon suffers a significant stroke, undergoes surgery for cerebral bleeding, and his authorities are transferred to deputy Ehud Olmert.
2006-01-05: Ariel Sharon's condition was greeted with deep concern by the Bush administration, and Condoleezza Rice praised him as "a wonderful, historic leader."
Ariel Sharon's almost certain withdrawal from office would leave a vacuum at the heart of Israeli government, raising questions about his possible successors.
Ariel Sharon is in intensive care after seven hours of emergency surgery to stop massive, widespread bleeding in his brain following a stroke.
2006-01-06: Ariel Sharon is succeeded by an unspecified successor amid uncertainty over his political future after he abandoned Likud to form a new party for March elections.
Doctors treating Ariel Sharon said a second round of emergency brain surgery had resulted in a significant improvement in the Israeli prime minister's condition.
2006-01-09: Ariel Sharon's doctors plan to begin bringing the Israeli prime minister out of his medically induced coma to assess brain damage caused by a stroke.
2006-01-10: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon showed improvement in his recovery from a major stroke, moving his left arm in response to stimulation, though doctors said it would still be days before they could assess whether he had lost his ability to think and reason.
2006-01-13: US TV evangelist Pat Robertson apologised to Ariel Sharon's family for suggesting Sharon's stroke was God's punishment for withdrawing from Gaza.
2006-01-14: Doctors treating Ariel Sharon are concerned that the Israeli prime minister has failed to show signs of emerging from a coma despite being taken off anaesthesia.
2006-01-16: Relatives of Ariel Sharon claimed he opened his eyes, but doctors treating him played down the report, and he remained in a coma since suffering a stroke almost two weeks earlier.
2006-02-11: Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon underwent emergency surgery to remove about 50 cm of his large intestine after an abdominal scan revealed severe damage to his digestive tract; he was in critical but stable condition with no immediate danger to his life.
2006-02-12: Ariel Sharon was in critical but stable condition after surgeons removed a decayed section of his large intestine, with doctors saying his chances of recovering from a massive stroke have dimmed.
2006-03-06: The director of the Jerusalem hospital treating Ariel Sharon says there is a chance the comatose Israeli prime minister could regain consciousness, though the chances are not great and his condition if he wakes remains an open question.
2006-03-28: Likud suffers a crushing defeat in Israeli elections, falling to fifth place with 11 seats, a result attributed in part to Ariel Sharon's earlier departure from the party to form Kadima.
Kadima, the party founded by Ariel Sharon, wins the most seats in Israel's general election, though fewer than expected, with acting Prime Minister Ehud Olmert beginning coalition talks.
2006-04-11: The Israeli cabinet declared Ariel Sharon permanently incapacitated, formally ending his term as prime minister and formalizing Ehud Olmert's role as acting prime minister.
2006-05-24: Ariel Sharon, comatose since January after a stroke, is to be moved to a long-term care centre next week, according to a hospital statement.
2007-01-04: A year after suffering a brain haemorrhage that left him in a persistent vegetative state, Ariel Sharon's political legacy is described as under siege, with his Gaza withdrawal and Kadima party facing criticism and his successor Ehud Olmert struggling.
2010-11-12: Former Israeli prime minister Ariel Sharon, in a coma for almost five years, was taken home to his ranch in the western Negev.
2014-01-01: Former Israeli prime minister Ariel Sharon's medical condition has deteriorated significantly, with reports saying death could come in a matter of days.
2014-01-03: Ariel Sharon died after being in a coma since a stroke in 2006.
2014-01-11: Former Israeli Prime Minister Ariel Sharon dies at age 85, eight years after a stroke left him in a coma.
2014-01-12: Ariel Sharon's legacy is assessed following his death, focusing on his divisive role in Israeli politics, including the West Bank separation barrier, settlements, and the Gaza disengagement.
2014-01-13: Ariel Sharon was laid to rest in a family ceremony at his ranch near the Negev desert, following a state memorial at the Knesset and a military service at Latrun.
Ariel Sharon's death is marked by an obituary and critical letters assessing his legacy, including the 1982 Sabra and Chatila refugee camp massacre and the 2005 Gaza withdrawal.
